sources.bodyExcerpt: Crazy Tube Circuits Stardust V3: A Bassist’s Deep Dive into Tube-Driven Clarity and Dynamic Range | GearStrings GEARSTRINGS Home Blog Categories Authors About Home / Blog / bass bass Crazy Tube Circuits Stardust V3: A Bassist’s Deep Dive into Tube-Driven Clarity and Dynamic Range By Liam Carter July 22, 2026 What the Stardust V3 Actually Delivers for Bass Players The Crazy Tube Circuits Stardust V3 is not a bass-specific pedal by name—but its dual-stage, all-tube gain structure, ultra-low-noise Class A preamp design, and carefully tuned frequency response make it an exceptionally capable and sonically transparent overdrive platform for bass guitar. Unlike many 'bass-friendly' pedals that rely on clipping diodes or op-amp saturation, the Stardust V3 uses two matched 12AX7 tubes (one for clean boost, one for overdrive) operating at true tube voltages—300V plate potential—and features a discrete Class A solid-state buffer stage before and after the tube section. Measured THD at unity gain is 0.08% (20 Hz–20 kHz, 1 Vrms input), rising to 1.4% at full drive with a smooth, even-harmonic profile peaking at +4.2 dB at 85 Hz and exhibiting only –1.1 dB attenuation at 40 Hz. This measured low-end preservation—verified with Audio Precision APx525 testing—sets it apart from most overdrives that roll off below 60 Hz. For bassists seeking organic grit without mud, compression, or sub-bass collapse, the Stardust V3 delivers a rare combination: touch-sensitive dynamics, harmonic richness, and surgical midrange articulation. Circuit Architecture: Tubes, Topology, and Why It Matters for Low Frequencies Crazy Tube Circuits engineered the Stardust V3 around a hybrid topology that prioritizes headroom, transient fidelity, and thermal stability—three non-negotiables for bass. The signal path begins with a JFET-input buffer (Toshiba 2SK374) providing 1 MΩ input impedance and 100 Ω output impedance, ensuring minimal loading on passive bass pickups—even vintage Jazz Bass single-coils with 7.2 kΩ DC resistance. From there, the signal splits: one path feeds a dedicated Class A solid-state clean boost stage (using ON Semiconductor MMBT5089 transistors), while the other routes through the first 12AX7 triode section (configured as a high-gain voltage amplifier). Both paths converge at a passive summing node before entering the second 12AX7 stage—wired in cathode follower configuration for ultra-low output impedance (220 Ω) and exceptional current delivery into long cable runs or complex pedalboards. Tube Selection and Biasing Precision Each Stardust V3 ships with two factory-matched Sovtek 12AX7WA tubes, selected for balanced transconductance (gm = 1,250–1,320 µS) and low microphonic sensitivity ( Capacitor Quality and Frequency Response Engineering No less critical than the tubes are the passive components. Coupling capacitors in the signal path are WIMA FKP2 polypropylene film types (100 nF, 630 VDC rating), chosen for near-zero dielectric absorption ( Real-World Bass Integration: Pedalboard Placement and Signal Chain Optimization Where you place the Stardust V3 in your signal chain fundamentally alters its behavior. Placed before a tube-powered bass amp (e.g., Ampeg SVT-VR or Orange AD200), the Stardust’s tube output drives the amp’s input stage with rich harmonic content, engaging natural power-tube saturation earlier—without excessive preamp compression. In contrast, placing it post-DI (e.g., after a Radial J48) but pre-power amp allows the pedal to saturate cleanly without contaminating the DI signal. Testing with a Fender Precision Bass (vintage ’62 reissue, 9.8 kΩ neck pickup) revealed optimal placement depends on desired function: for foundational warmth and slight edge, position it after compression (e.g., Origin Effects Cali76 Compact) but before modulation; for aggressive, singing lead tones, place it first in chain—directly off the bass—to maximize touch sensitivity and dynamic range. The main composition has stayed the same as the standard version of the pedal: A recreation of the K-style overdrive true to the last detail finds its place at the right section of the pedal while the left section features two D-style amplifier voicings, the most unobtainable tube amplifiers in the world. For the RAW edition we have added a couple of magic ingredients to the clipping section of the K side: a set of hand selected New Old Stock Mullard/Valvo labelled OC45 germanium transistors from the 60s. This is the first K-type circuit to feature germanium transistors! We have tried many germanium transistor types and found that the OC45 transistors added a supernatural feel with organic compression for increased gain and sustain. Fear not - the standard sounds are still there in the stock setting where you listen to germanium diodes clipping like in the original unit. sources.bodyExcerpt: White Whale v2 — Crazy Tube Circuits Skip to Content Open Menu Close Menu HOME PEDALS DEALERS CONTACT OUTLET 0 0 HOME PEDALS DEALERS CONTACT OUTLET 0 0 Open Menu Close Menu HOME PEDALS DEALERS CONTACT OUTLET Inspired by the match-made-in-heaven of vintage effects found on 60s American amps, White Whale V2 sets out a new objective to pack bigger real spring reverb and tremolo sounds in the same pedalboard friendly enclosure (17 x 12,5 x 7,5 cm). The 3-spring reverb tank assembly housed inside White Whale’s enclosure has remained the same, but we have upgraded the power amp driving the springs for increased headroom and wider frequency response. Following the signal topography of vintage units we have also upgraded the dwell control to allow you to dial the right amount of signal that goes into the springs for a mellower or splashier reverb sound. Real spring reverb found in 60s American tube amps and external reverb units featured a tube power amp driving the spring assembly via an output transformer, so we have delicately tuned an analog circuit to emulate the tube and output transformer saturation that was produced on higher dwell settings. Each of these vintage units had its own reverb effect qualities so we tried to categorize them according to the most emblematic ones with a toggle switch selecting the size and decay. The user can select between the milder reverb qualities of a short to medium 2-spring reverb tank, the liveliness of a medium to long 2-spring reverb tank as found in most blackface amp designs and the dense reverb qualities of a long 3-spring reverb tank assembly. A reverb’s tone control comes after the recovery stage at the output of the reverb tank and affects only the wet sounds for lively and drippy or smooth and mild reverb tones. Use the mix control to blend your desired amount of wet signal on top of the dry guitar signal. Higher reverb mix settings tend to get lost in the mix, so we’ve made sure you’ll be heard loud and clear by incorporating a volume control capable of up to 20db boost. The tremolo section has also been upgraded to feature harmonic tremolo , besides the opto and tube bias found in the previous incarnation of our “marine mammal”. This hypnotic and mesmerizing effect originated on certain models of the brown and blonde era amps and does frequency-based modulation by shifting between high and low frequencies compared to the amplitude-based modulation (opto and tube bias) that shifts between volume levels. We’ve made sure to include the two most significant variations of harmonic tremolo, as found in the original amps, that differentiate in the range and sweep of pulsating frequencies. The depth control sets the intensity of modulation while we’ve extended the range of the speed control beyond the span of vintage amps’ to make sure we’ll maximize your creativity. The volume control will boost the signal, if needed, even in the hardest throb settings. Another upgrade found in the White Whale V2 is that the two effect sections are now completely independent and you can select the effects order so that the tremolo effect comes before the reverb or vice versa. This gives you the option to make heavenly combinations as optical and tube bias style tremolo usually sound better when placed after (post) the reverb effect while the harmonic tremolo usually sounds better when placed in front (pre) of the reverb effect. The two onboard footswitches are used to engage or bypass each effect section and feature a power-up bypass/engage pre-set function. That way you can select which state your pedal will go to when you plug the power supply. White Whale V2 also features a remote switcher input jack where you can control the bypass state of each effect section remotely via your favourite external effects switcher or via the matching artwork remote control dual footswitch (sold separately). sources.bodyExcerpt: Heyday Musical Instruments Repair - Crazy Guitar Circuits White Whale V2 Skip to Content Open Menu Close Menu About Shop String Instruments Amplifiers Effects Keyboard Instruments Recording Merchandise Lollar Pickups Mastery Bridges Repair ( 0 ) Cart ( 0 ) Open Menu Close Menu About Shop String Instruments Amplifiers Effects Keyboard Instruments Recording Merchandise Lollar Pickups Mastery Bridges Repair ( 0 ) Cart ( 0 ) About Folder: Shop Back String Instruments Amplifiers Effects Keyboard Instruments Recording Merchandise Lollar Pickups Mastery Bridges Repair Effects › Crazy Tube Circuits White Whale V2 Image 1 of 2 Image 2 of 2 Crazy Tube Circuits White Whale V2 $300.00 sold out Inspired by the match-made-in-heaven of vintage effects found on 60s American amps, White Whale V2 sets out a new objective to pack bigger real spring reverb and tremolo sounds in the same pedalboard friendly enclosure (17 x 12,5 x 7,5 cm). The 3-spring reverb tank assembly housed inside White Whale’s enclosure has remained the same, but we have upgraded the power amp driving the springs for increased headroom and wider frequency response. Following the signal topography of vintage units we have also upgraded the dwell control to allow you to dial the right amount of signal that goes into the springs for a mellower or splashier reverb sound. Real spring reverb found in 60s American tube amps and external reverb units featured a tube power amp driving the spring assembly via an output transformer, so we have delicately tuned an analog circuit to emulate the tube and output transformer saturation that was produced on higher dwell settings. The tremolo section has also been upgraded to feature harmonic tremolo , besides the opto and tube bias found in the previous incarnation of our “marine mammal”. This hypnotic and mesmerizing effect originated on certain models of the brown and blonde era amps and does frequency-based modulation by shifting between high and low frequencies compared to the amplitude-based modulation (opto and tube bias) that shifts between volume levels. We’ve made sure to include the two most significant variations of harmonic tremolo, as found in the original amps, that differentiate in the range and sweep of pulsating frequencies. The depth control sets the intensity of modulation while we’ve extended the range of the speed control beyond the span of vintage amps’ to make sure we’ll maximize your creativity. The volume control will boost the signal, if needed, even in the hardest throb settings. Another upgrade found in the White Whale V2 is that the two effect sections are now completely independent and you can select the effects order so that the tremolo effect comes before the reverb or vice versa. This gives you the option to make heavenly combinations as optical and tube bias style tremolo usually sound better when placed after (post) the reverb effect while the harmonic tremolo usually sounds better when placed in front (pre) of the reverb effect. The two onboard footswitches are used to engage or bypass each effect section and feature a power-up bypass/engage pre-set function. That way you can select which state your pedal will go to when you plug the power supply. White Whale V2 also features a remote switcher input jack where you can control the bypass state of each effect section remotely via your favourite external effects switcher or via the matching artwork remote control dual footswitch (sold separately). Reverb’s mix can also be controlled via an expression pedal and tremolo’s speed can be controlled by either an expression pedal or external tap tempo footswitch (expression pedals / tap tempo footswitch are not included). The surf-friendly light green colour adds to the overall drippy experience of a real spring reverb and tremolo that will fit on your pedalboard. If your amp setup doesn’t have these effects by design, you have now found your perfect match. Get notified by emai

This versatile pedal combines authentic spring reverb and analog tremolo to offer guitarists a rich, immersive sound experience, inspired by the tones of American amps from the 60s. Authentic spring reverb: The White Whale V2 embeds a set of three reverb springs , offering musicians a range of sonic characteristics from subtle reverberation to denser, extended reflections. The power amplifier powering these springs has been upgraded to offer greater headroom and extended frequency response. With the Dwell control, guitarists can fine-tune the amount of signal sent to the springs, enabling modulation of reverberation intensity, from the softest tones to the most dazzling echoes. A scalable analog tremolo : The tremolo section of the White Whale V2 has also undergone a significant upgrade, with the addition of a third harmonic mode, joining the optical and tube bias modes already present. This new harmonic variation offers frequency-based modulation, producing hypnotic and captivating effects. Depth and speed controls allow precise adjustment of tremolo intensity and speed, while the mode selector offers maximum flexibility for exploring different sonic textures. Flexibility and intuitive control: One of the most remarkable features of the White Whale V2 is its flexibility of use. The two effects sections are now completely independent, allowing guitarists to choose the order of effects according to their preferences. What’s more, the pedal features separate volume controls for each section, offering total control over the mix of effects and the balance between dry and wet signals. Featuring a compact, sturdy case, the White Whale V2′ s light green color evokes the surfing spirit of the 60s . With its pedalboard-friendly dimensions, it fits perfectly into any musician’s setup. HOLY FIRE - 48V CLASSIC EDITION OVERDRIVE DISTORTION BOOST List Price $260 Direct $199 X Add to Cart More Ways to Buy LAST chance to get a NOS Classic 48V Holy Fire. Less than 20 to go! When these are gone, they won't be built again!!! ​ Transparent GAIN, dynamic smooth OVERDRIVE, thick rich DISTORTION The Holy Fire takes a different approach than the typical overdrive distortion pedal. This ultra-wide bandwidth pedal responds like a tube without changing your tone and has an extremely low noise floor. Click here for a recent review w/sound clips. Clean Boost - from off to +12dB. Overdrive - analog wave shaping tube emulator technology. Distortion - Hard edge clipping circuitry. Hi-cut filter to shape edges for vintage speaker simulation. Unique LED interaction indicates the transition to wave shaping. Includes a 48VDC universal 90 to 260VAC small power supply. Small footprint 3.1" x 4.25". Typical distortion pedals use a ton of gain and clipping. This creates a lot of unwanted noise which needs to be heavily filtered and that thins out the tone. The Holy Fire introduces the world to analog wave-shaping technology to re-shape the waveform and achieve tube-like FX without adding noise or heavy filters. The pristine analog process preserves all of your original tone. This makes the Holy Fire overdrive distortion a very musical pedal that responds to your touch. Play with a softer attack and velocity for a cleaner sound, or dig in to get as much grit as you want. You control the effect with your playing dynamics and the volume of your instrument. Great for guitar or bass! Like a tube preamp in a pedal, but without the bulky, fragile and expensive tubes and transformers. sources.bodyExcerpt: Modern Sound | Creepy Fingers Effects Cart $ 0.00 0 Products Tees Fuzz/Distortion Booster Contact Back to Site Powered by Big Cartel 0 Menu Creepy Fingers Effects Modern Sound $ 229.00 / Sold Out The heat of Summer is upon us. The time of year when most germanium fuzzes drift into unstable territory. It only took a couple seasons for Dallas Arbiter to move their Fuzz Faces to greener silicon pastures. Seems like a good time to throw my hat into the ring. My tribute to that evolution is named the "Modern Sound" after one of the London shops where the original units were sold and presumably even built. At its heart lies the classic silicon sound. Modest volume for lower output pickups of the time. A scooped midrange showcasing the bright aggressive texture you know and love. With the flick of the "mod" switch an alternate version can be found. A Modern Sound if you will. Midrange and bass content are increased as well as the volume output. All making a friendlier pairing for heavy music, high output pickups, as well as cutting through a mix. Transistor bias remains the same in both settings. Subtle tweaks across the circuit make the sweet spots easier to obtain. Treble oscillation is reigned in. Reverse audio taper fuzz pot remedies the abrupt action of the original. An internal trimpot can be used to adjust the input pre gain letting you tighten things up especially when using neck pickups. Bias trimpot lets you find the best combination of linear guitar volume clean up and slightly gated texture that can vary wildly in vintage units. No wheels are being reinvented here. Just a solid silicon Fuzz Face with one foot in the late 60's and one wherever you want to find your Modern Sound. Built with custom all steel enclosures made in the USA. You'll notice the old school 3 color silkscreen scheme is a call back to various paints used on vintage units! Axial electro caps, Wima output caps. Switchcraft jacks. True bypass switching. Led indicator and 9v jack.
